title: Completed-base tensor comparison at primes containing the adic ideal
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset R$ an ideal, and $U$ a finite-type commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $H=\varprojlim_jR/I^j$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $W=H\otimes_R U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with its canonical maps from $H$ and $U$. For a prime $\mathfrak r\subset U$ containing $IU$, let $\mathfrak n\subset W$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak r/IU$ under the canonical isomorphism $W/IW\cong U/IU$. Put $Z=U_{\mathfrak r}$ and $W_*=W_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and write $\mathfrak m_Z,\mathfrak m_{W_*}$ for their maximal ideals. Then $W$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak m_{W_*}=\mathfrak m_ZW_*$, and the canonical local map $Z\to W_*$ induces for every $j\ge1$ an isomorphism
$$Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j\xrightarrow{\sim}W_*/\mathfrak m_{W_*}^j.$$
Its inverse sends the class of a completed coefficient $\hat r$ times $u$ to $ru$, with $r\in R$ any representative of the $j$th coordinate of $\hat r\in\varprojlim_jR/I^j$; localized denominators are sent to their inverses. These isomorphisms commute with reduction in $j$, identify the residue fields, and induce a continuous isomorphism with continuous inverse
$$\widehat Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{W_*}$$
which commutes with the maps from $U$. The ideal $I$ need not be maximal and $R$ need not be local.

proof.text: The tensor algebra structure is the one in the cited universal-property statement. In particular the factor interchange $U\otimes_RH\to H\otimes_RU$, $u\otimes h\mapsto h\otimes u$, is a ring isomorphism: the reverse formula is inverse on pure tensors, which generate. We use this identification below. The completion-Noetherian theorem gives that $H$ is Noetherian. If $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ generate $U$ over $R$, the elements $1\otimes u_i$ generate $W$ over $H$: expand each $u$ as a polynomial in the $u_i$ and each tensor as a finite sum of pure tensors. The finite-type Noetherian theorem applied to $H\to W$ therefore proves that $W$ is Noetherian.

proof.text: Since $R$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated. The completion-mod-power statement gives $\pi_j:H\to R/I^j$, surjective with kernel $I^jH$ and with the required composite from $R$. Apply the tensor quotient lemma with $B=H$, $C=U$ and any ideal $J\supseteq IU$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $U/J^j\to W/J^jW$ whose inverse sends $[h\otimes u]$ to $[ru]$, where $r$ represents $\pi_j(h)$. In particular $J=IU$, $j=1$ constructs the stated identification $W/IW\cong U/IU$; here $(IU)W=IW$ because both ideals are generated by the images of elements of $I$. Taking $J=\mathfrak r$ gives isomorphisms $\alpha_j:U/\mathfrak r^j\to W/\mathfrak r^jW$ for all $j\geq1$.

source.place: Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); explicit assembly supplied by Q47.

proof.text: Let $f:U\to W$ be the canonical map. The prime $\mathfrak n$ is the inverse image of the prime $\mathfrak r/IU$ under $W\to W/IW\cong U/IU$, hence is prime, and $f^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak r$, since the composite from $U$ is its quotient map. Apply the prime-power localization lemma to $f$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak r$, $Q=\mathfrak n$ and the $\alpha_j$ from Step 2. It gives $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak rW$ and the compatible canonical local quotient isomorphisms $e_j:Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j\to W_*/\mathfrak m_{W_*}^j$. The maximal ideals are $\mathfrak rZ$ and $\mathfrak nW_*$ by the localization definition, so $\mathfrak m_{W_*}=\mathfrak m_ZW_*$: both are generated in $W_*$ by $f(\mathfrak r)$.

source.place: Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); explicit assembly supplied by Q47.

proof.text: The inverse formula of Step 2 descends to the local inverse: first map $w\in W$ to its inverse image under $\alpha_j$, then to $Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j$. For $t\notin\mathfrak n$, lift its class modulo $\mathfrak r^jW$ to $c\in U$ using $\alpha_j$. Then $t-f(c)\in\mathfrak r^jW\subseteq\mathfrak n$ and $c\notin\mathfrak r$ by contraction. Thus its image is a unit in $Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j$, with inverse the image of $1/c\in Z$. Send $[w/t]$ to the image of $w$ times that unit inverse. This is inverse to $e_j$, since applying $e_j$ recovers $[w/t]$. For $w=h\otimes u$ this is exactly the stated coefficient formula. A different representative $r$ changes $ru$ by an element of $I^jU\subseteq\mathfrak r^j$, so gives the same answer.

proof.text: The transition compatibility of the $e_j$ was supplied in Step 3. It also holds for their inverses: multiply the equality of the two transition composites by $e_j^{-1}$ and $e_k^{-1}$. The case $j=1$ identifies the residue fields, since these are exactly the maximal-ideal quotients of $Z$ and $W_*$, and $e_1$ is induced by the canonical local map.

proof.text: Write both completions as compatible sequences of maximal-ideal residues. Send $(z_j)_j$ to $(e_j(z_j))_j$ and send $(w_j)_j$ back to $(e_j^{-1}(w_j))_j$. Step 5 shows that these sequences are compatible. Componentwise operations make these ring homomorphisms, and the two composites are identities in every coordinate, hence identities on the completions. For $u\in U$, the $j$th coordinate of its image on either side is the image of $u$ under the canonical local map modulo $\mathfrak m_{W_*}^j$. This proves commutation with the maps from $U$.

source.place: Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); explicit assembly supplied by Q47.

proof.text: For continuity, the localization-Noetherian theorem makes $Z=U_{\mathfrak r}$ and $W_*=W_{\mathfrak n}$ Noetherian: $U$ is Noetherian by the finite-type theorem over $R$, and $W$ is Noetherian by Step 1. Their maximal ideals are therefore finitely generated. The completion-mod-power theorem applied to these two ideals identifies the kernels of the $j$th completion projections with $\mathfrak m_Z^j\widehat Z$ and $\mathfrak m_{W_*}^j\widehat{W_*}$ respectively. These ideal powers are the basic neighborhoods of zero for the respective completed adic topologies. The coordinatewise map of Step 6 carries each first kernel onto the corresponding second kernel, because $e_j$ is injective, and its inverse does the reverse. Thus both maps are continuous at zero, and translation gives continuity everywhere.
